title: A Garden for the Songbook
premise: Theo Pemberton, a wedding planner who stopped believing in love after his own engagement collapsed, has spent three years living carefully in the coastal town of Marrow Bay, tending a neglected garden he inherited from his grandmother. When Wren Okafor—the stranger who wrote him anonymous letters for a decade, letters that once saved his life—moves into the cottage next door, Theo must decide whether to keep hiding behind routine or risk being truly known. As the last ferry of the season approaches, Wren's own secret reason for coming threatens to unravel them both: she is the estranged daughter of the man whose negligence killed Theo's sister, seeking justice her family buried. Choosing each other over vengeance and safety, they stay past the final crossing, restoring the garden together as a living songbook of everyone they've lost and found.
about_author: Vesper Delacroix is the pen name of a former florist who spent ten years writing letters to strangers before turning to fiction. She lives on a windswept peninsula where the ferries stop running in winter.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry Schedule
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He plans a flawless wedding for clients while privately cataloguing all the ways love fails, then walks home past the ferry dock and notes the season's final departure date pinned to the board. The beat: controlled loneliness, a life measured in safe increments.

chapters.title: Letters I Never Answered
chapters.summary: Flashback woven through present-day Theo sorting his grandmother's attic. We learn about the decade of unsigned letters that arrived after his sister Ivy's death—each one quoting a garden plant like a verse. The beat: grief given shape, mystery planted.

chapters.title: A Moving Van in November
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She arrives at the neighboring cottage off-season, watched by Theo from behind his hedge. Her interiority reveals she chose this town deliberately but not why. The beat: wary curiosity, two guarded people measuring each other across a fence line.

chapters.title: Borrowed Sugar, Borrowed Time
chapters.summary: Wren knocks asking for sugar; Theo, socially rusty, over-prepares and under-delivers. Their awkward first real conversation reveals her knowledge of gardening and his defensive charm. The beat: comic tenderness, first crack in his armor.

chapters.title: What the Garden Remembers
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He begins restoring his grandmother's overgrown beds and finds Wren already there at dawn pulling bindweed without being asked. She quotes a phrase—one of the letter lines—casually. The beat: vertigo, suspicion blooming alongside attraction.

chapters.title: The Wedding That Wasn't
chapters.summary: A client's wedding collapses when the couple calls it off mid-rehearsal, and Theo handles it with devastating grace while privately unraveling. Wren finds him afterward on the empty beach. The beat: exposure—he sees she sees him.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Tuesdays
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Alone, she rereads her own drafts of the letters, revealing she wrote them as penance for something unnamed tied to her father. The beat: her guilt established, stakes raised, reader ahead of Theo now.

chapters.title: First Frost, First Confession
chapters.summary: Trapped by a storm in Theo's greenhouse, Wren admits she knows about Ivy—not how, just that she does—and Theo storms out. The beat: betrayal felt before explanation, the romance's first true rupture.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: Theo discovers his grandmother's will left the garden to 'whoever keeps it singing,' a clause his uncle is contesting in court to sell the land. The beat: external threat crystallized—belonging made legal, and therefore fragile.

chapters.title: Depositions and Dahlias
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Theo preps for the custody-of-the-garden hearing while Wren quietly researches property law, revealing an unnerving fluency. The beat: alliance rebuilt through shared purpose rather than apology.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signed Nothing
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. We learn her father's construction company cut corners on the site where Ivy died, and that she spent a decade writing to survivors because he never would. The beat: her full secret laid bare to the reader, dread building toward Theo's discovery.

chapters.title: Everything Blooms Twice
chapters.summary: A tender interlude: the pair plant spring bulbs together, trade truths that aren't the truth, and nearly kiss before Theo pulls back. The beat: hope, and the audience screaming at the page.

chapters.title: Found Among the Papers
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Helping Wren unpack, he finds a box of letter drafts in her handwriting. The revelation lands: his lifeline for ten years was written by the daughter of the man who killed his sister. The beat: the floor giving way.

chapters.title: Winter Without Ferries
chapters.summary: Theo cuts Wren off completely; the town closes in for the off-season and his isolation becomes total. His uncle leverages the scandal to fast-track the sale. The beat: rock bottom dressed as safety.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: In court, Theo's uncle argues sentiment means nothing; Theo, unprepared, freezes—until Wren appears in the gallery, having subpoenaed records showing the land's covenant protects community gardens. The beat: justice outside the law begins inside it.

chapters.title: Cross-Examination of the Heart
chapters.summary: Wren testifies about the garden's role in the town, publicly linking herself to Theo and exposing her father's company in the process. Her family disowns her by phone within the hour. The beat: sacrifice made visible, cost counted.

chapters.title: What You Owe and What You're Owed
chapters.summary: Theo confronts Wren at the dock: was any of it real, or was he a project? She answers with the one thing she never put in a letter—that writing to him was the only honest thing she'd ever done. The beat: fury transmuting into understanding.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Climax. Wren stands at the terminal with a ticket, believing leaving is her penance completed. Theo runs the length of the seawall and asks her to stay—not forgiven, but chosen. The boat leaves without her. The beat: the blurb's promise fulfilled.

chapters.title: Reading Aloud
chapters.summary: Quiet aftermath chapter. Theo reads her every letter aloud in the greenhouse, finally answering each one after ten years, and they grieve Ivy together properly for the first time. The beat: catharsis, intimacy built from honesty.

chapters.title: The Uncle's Retreat
chapters.summary: Facing the covenant evidence and town pressure, Theo's uncle withdraws the contest; the garden is secured. Theo realizes belonging was never granted by documents but by the people who showed up. The beat: victory, understated.

chapters.title: A Wedding, After All
chapters.summary: The couple whose wedding collapsed asks Theo to plan their elopement in the restored garden. He says yes, and planning it heals something he didn't know was still broken. Wren helps, her hands in the same soil. The beat: belief cautiously reborn.

chapters.title: Spring Planting
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating POVs. One year later, the garden blooms as a living songbook—each bed labeled with a name and a line from a letter. Theo plants a new row marked simply 'us.' The beat: inheritance redefined, belonging earned, home chosen.
